NJ-04.label: Absorption thin
NJ-04.text: The project needs about 30% of unmet demand in its 7-mile market (38% if Woodmont's approved Parsippany building goes ahead). The combined downside holds with a GMP, about $1.2M of cushion; the redevelopment designation makes a PILOT available to widen it. NIC MAP pull and pre-leasing plan before LOI.

NJ-06.label: Hold: absorption
NJ-06.text: Arbor Terrace Florham Park (80 AL/MC, opening late 2027) uses up most of the unmet demand this pad needs. Hold behind Florham Park; do not pursue both.

NY-03.label: Partner role · PILOT + fee
NY-03.text: VS Construction controls the site and Benchmark is the prospective operator, so ATCO's role is capital or GC. Fully taxed YOC is 5.84% with comp-based rents and building size; a PILOT lifts it to 6.68%, but the combined downside holds only for a tax-exempt owner.

NY-01.label: Fee development only (pending ATCO)
NY-01.text: Entrance-fee coverage is 70%, right at the screen, so the verdict flips with small input changes. A for-profit owner loses about $14.6M even with entrance fees; a nonprofit sponsor makes about $18.3M, and ATCO earns about a $6.9M development fee plus the GC contract. Sunrise is the contract vendee.

NY-10.label: Dropped: rents not supported
NY-10.text: No Dutchess AL listing is above $6,000 a month and the area average is about $5,000. At a comp-based $6,820 the site falls below 6.5% under every structure.

CT-02.label: Entrance-fee campus only
CT-02.text: As a rental it misses even with a PILOT (6.17%). As an entrance-fee life plan, fees cover 73% of IL cost; a nonprofit sponsor case makes about $28.9M and ATCO's development fee is about $4.9M.

NJ-10.label: Needs a PILOT
NJ-10.text: With comp-based building size, fully taxed YOC is 6.45%, just under the floor. It clears with a PILOT, but no redevelopment designation was found for Brookside; Montville's past PILOTs came through affordable-housing settlements. Ask the township before LOI.
